statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. Define an integer i to be good when: (1) k <= i < n-k; (2) for every t with i-k <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1]; and (3) for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k, nums[t] <= nums[t+1]. Then r is exactly the increasing list of all good integers: for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), r[p] is good and there are exactly p good integers smaller than r[p]; also, for every good integer i there is exactly one p with 0 <= p < len(r) and r[p] = i. In particular, len(r) is the number of good integers.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or perform an out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every element of r is a valid candidate index: for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), k <= r[p] < n-k.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, its entries are strictly increasing in position: for every p and q with 0 <= p < q < len(r), r[p] < r[q]. In particular, r contains no duplicates.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every returned index is good. That is, for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), with i = r[p], we have k <= i < n-k, for every t with i-k <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1], and for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k, nums[t] <= nums[t+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every good index is present in r. That is, for every integer i with k <= i < n-k, if for every t with i-k <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1], and for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k, nums[t] <= nums[t+1], then there exists p with 0 <= p < len(r) and r[p] = i.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of good indices, i.e. the number of integers i for which k <= i < n-k, for every t with i-k <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1], and for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k, nums[t] <= nums[t+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= len(r) <= n-2*k.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is empty: len(r) = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000; and n = 2*k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the list of all interior indices in increasing order: len(r) = n-2 and for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), r[p] = p+1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000; and k = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the increasing list of all candidate indices: len(r) = n-2*k and for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), r[p] = k+p.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000; and all entries of nums are equal, i.e. there exists an integer c with nums[j] = c for every 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a nonempty result r, r[0] is the smallest good index and r[len(r)-1] is the largest good index, where an integer i is good when k <= i < n-k, for every t with i-k <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1], and for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k, nums[t] <= nums[t+1]. Formally: r[0] is good and r[0] <= i for every good integer i; r[len(r)-1] is good and i <= r[len(r)-1] for every good integer i.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the returned indices remain good for every smaller positive window. More precisely, for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), for every integer k' with 1 <= k' <= k, if i = r[p], then k' <= i < n-k', for every t with i-k' <= t < i-1, nums[t] >= nums[t+1], and for every t with i+1 <= t < i+k', nums[t] <= nums[t+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the same r is the exact increasing list of good indices for any other slice nums' of length n that has the same adjacent comparison pattern. More precisely, let nums' be any integer slice with len(nums') = n and such that for every t with 0 <= t < n-1, nums[t] < nums[t+1] iff nums'[t] < nums'[t+1], and nums[t] = nums[t+1] iff nums'[t] = nums'[t+1]. Then for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), r[p] is good with respect to nums' (same definition with nums' in place of nums), and every integer that is good with respect to nums' occurs in r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). All arithmetic in this specification is mathematical integer arithmetic and all indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= k and 2*k <= n (equivalently k <= floor(n/2)); for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000.
